verses.text: My brothers and sisters, you believe in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ, so do not treat some people better than others.
Suppose a man comes into your meeting wearing a gold ring and fine clothes, and a poor man in dirty clothes also comes in.
You pay special attention to the man in fine clothes and say, "Please sit here in this good seat." But you say to the poor man, "Stand over there," or "Sit on the floor by my feet."
Then you are treating people differently, and you are judging them with evil thoughts.
Listen, my dear brothers and sisters. God chose people who are poor in this world to be rich in faith. They will receive the kingdom he promised to those who love him.
But you have shamed the poor! Is it not the rich who treat you badly and drag you into court?
Are they not the ones who insult the good name of Jesus, to whom you belong?
It is good if you really keep the royal law found in the Scriptures: "Love your neighbour as you love yourself."
But if you treat some people better than others, you are sinning. The law shows that you are guilty of breaking it.
Whoever keeps the whole law but fails in just one point is guilty of breaking all of it.
God said, "Do not cheat on your marriage." He also said, "Do not murder." So if you do not cheat on your marriage but you do murder, you have still broken the law.
Speak and act like people who will be judged by the law that sets us free.
Anyone who has not shown mercy will be judged without mercy. But mercy wins over judgment.
My brothers and sisters, what good is it if someone says they have faith, but they do not show it by what they do? Can that kind of faith save them?
Suppose a brother or sister has no clothes and no food for the day.
If one of you says to them, "Go in peace. Keep warm and eat well," but you do not give them what they need, what good is that?
In the same way, faith by itself, if it does not lead to action, is dead.
But someone will say, "You have faith, and I have actions." Show me your faith without actions, and I will show you my faith by what I do.
You believe there is one God. Good! Even the demons believe that, and they shake with fear.
You foolish person, do you want proof that faith without actions is useless?
Our ancestor Abraham was made right with God by what he did, when he offered his son Isaac on the altar.
You see that his faith and his actions worked together. His faith was made complete by what he did.
So the Scripture came true that says, "Abraham believed God, and God accepted him as right with him." And Abraham was called God's friend.
So you see that a person is made right with God by what they do, and not by faith alone.
In the same way, Rahab the prostitute was made right with God by what she did. She welcomed the spies and sent them away by a different road.
Just as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without actions is dead.
